text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — multiple nodes in infer-pool (eu-west-1) flapping NotReady / kubelet restarts. Pods evicted and restarted; several inference pods report OOM and CUDA driver errors. Alerts: node-notready x3, pod-oom x6, cuda-driver-fail x2. Start: 2026-03-17T10:15:32Z

oncall-alex: Ack, I'm awake. joining incident.

eng-sre-maya: Which nodes? any pattern (hardware/driver)?

incident-bot: Nodes: infer-eu-01, infer-eu-04, infer-eu-07. All three showed kubelet restart within 90s. Kernel logs and kubelet show repeated "watchdog reset" on 10:14:58Z.

eng-infra-jordan: I'll take infra. Suspect NIC/driver or kernel watchdog on this batch of hosts. Recommend cordon+drain 1 node at a time.

oncall-alex: Agree. Need quick mitigation to stop client errors — routing is currently failing over and spiking latency. Can runtime reduce concurrency / batch to lower memory pressure?

eng-runtime-sam: Yes — we can push a temporary runtime override for that shard to reduce max_concurrency and batch_size. That should reduce per-pod memory and avoid OOMs during evacs.

eng-runtime-sam: Quick commands:
```bash
# lower batch tokens and max concurrency for model-route 'text-gen-prod'
redwoodctl routes set text-gen-prod --max_concurrency=1 --max_batch_tokens=128 --note="emergency: node flaps"
```

support-ryan: We're already getting customer reports: ticket #12345 and #12348 — increased 500s and latency ~10s for a subset of EU customers. They're asking for ETA.

product-ops-li: Can we update status page? simple message: "Investigating increased errors/latency for EU inference; mitigation in progress." Will draft customer note once we have ETA.

eng-sre-maya: Log snippet from one restarted pod: 
```
2026-03-17T10:13:01Z infer-runtime[pid]: runtime: panic: out of memory
2026-03-17T10:13:02Z infer-runtime[pid]: CUDA driver error: cuCtxCreate failed: unknown error (code=700)
```

eng-infra-jordan: Noted. I'll cordon infer-eu-07 and drain with graceful 120s, one at a time. Drain command:
```bash
kubectl cordon infer-eu-07 && kubectl drain infer-eu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

oncall-alex: Before drain, can we move traffic away from that zone? If autoscaler kicks, might create more churn.

eng-runtime-sam: I'm toggling routing policy to prefer fallback pool (dedicated-fallback-eu) for 5m to reduce pressure on infer-pool. Doing that now.

eng-runtime-sam: done — routing override applied :white_check_mark:

support-ryan: Confirmed reduction in customer 500s for those tickets. Thanks.

eng-infra-jordan: infer-eu-07 cordoned & drained. Reboots in progress. I'll watch driver logs during boot.

oncall-alex: I'm lowering model replicas for heavy models in eu-west to avoid re-scheduling spikes.

eng-runtime-sam: Also applied emergency config to runtime: 
```json
{"env_override":"INFER_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=64","note":"emergency node-flap mitigation"}
```
(we push via config service — should take ~30s)

eng-sre-maya: Observing fewer OOMs after the overrides. Pod restarts dropped from 6 -> 1 in the last 2m.

incident-bot: Update: infer-eu-07 rebooted, kernel boot shows watchdog reset at 10:14:58. Driver versions on node: nvidia-driver 530.41.03. Scheduling infer pods back slowly.

eng-infra-jordan: I'll run a hardware probe and keep infer-eu-01 and -04 cordoned until we confirm stability. Suspect flaky NIC/firmware causing kubelet watchdog. Opening infra ticket INFRA-3321.

product-ops-li: Drafted status page update and customer note. Posting in 10m unless we have a full fix sooner.

support-ryan: Escalating customer tickets with interim workaround: retry logic and reduced concurrency. Notifying impacted customers now.

oncall-alex: Any CUDA driver mismatches across nodes?

eng-infra-jordan: Checking cluster image — most nodes on 530.41, a few on 525.x. I'll standardize to 530.41 once we triage.

eng-runtime-sam: If nodes come back flaky, we should enable model CPU fallback for critical routes to avoid GPU driver issues. I can flip that per-route.

oncall-alex: Go ahead, enable CPU fallback for top-10 customers temporarily.

eng-runtime-sam: Enabled CPU fallback on top-10 routes. Monitoring perf impact.

eng-sre-maya: Monitoring dashboards show tail latency and error rate trending down. Still watching memory jitter on remaining nodes.

incident-bot: Summary/next steps: cordoned/drained infer-eu-07 (rebooted), infra investigating watchdog/kernel cause, runtime lowered batch/concurrency + routing override + CPU fallbacks enabled, support updating customers, product queued status page update.

oncall-alex: Good triage. Keep me posted. If nodes continue flapping, we'll initiate cross-region failover for critical flows.

eng-infra-jordan: I'll post infra findings in this thread when probes finish. ETA 30-45m.

support-ryan: Notifying customer success to coordinate comms.

eng-sre-maya: Monitoring for 15m stable window then we'll lift routing overrides and restore normal concurrency.

product-ops-li: Posting status now.

oncall-alex: Thank you all — keeping this thread as source of truth. :thumbsup:

eng-sre-maya: marking incident as "mitigating". Will update to "resolved" after 15m stable and infra confirms hardware/driver OK.
